claims.text: The target material is a multicomponent high-entropy material in a high-temperature state.
A machine-learning potential would be trained on ab initio data for the specific multicomponent material.
Incorporating the machine-learning potential can improve determination of the transition temperature.
Incorporating the machine-learning potential can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
Incorporating the machine-learning potential can improve determination of the volume change and dense-fluid heat capacity.
The machine-learning potential can accurately capture complex interactions in the multicomponent system.
Capturing those interactions permits efficient and accurate calculation of thermodynamic properties.
The machine-learning-potential approach will be more efficient than ab initio molecular dynamics.
The machine-learning-potential approach will be more accurate than classical molecular dynamics.
DFT free-energy studies and TOR-TILD are relevant existing computational baselines.
The proposed approach is applicable to high-temperature multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Performance may be limited by transferability across temperatures and compositions and by overfitting or underfitting.
Comparison against ab initio molecular dynamics and experimental measurements can test the proposed approach.
